title: Water Monitoring and Tracking Essential Resources (WATER) Data Improvement Act
official_summary:
Water Monitoring and Tracking Essential Resources (WATER) Data Improvement Act

This act reauthorizes through FY2028 the following initiatives of the United States Geological Survey (USGS): (1) Federal Priority Streamgage program (previously known as the National Streamflow Information Program); (2) groundwater monitoring program, including the National Groundwater Monitoring Network; and (3) grants for water estimation, measurement, and monitoring technologies and methodologies.

The act also modifies the Federal Priority Streamgage program, which measures and tracks the amount of water in nationally significant watersheds and provides information about those watersheds and their conditions, such as floods and droughts. Currently, the USGS must ensure that all streamgages are equipped with water-quality sensors. The act requires that those sensors are precipitation water-quality sensors. The act also requires each streamgage site to conform with the federal needs established through regular solicitation and feedback, such as that documented in the report titled Re-prioritization of the U.S. Geological Survey Federal Priority streamgage program, 2022.

summary.headline: Law extends three U.S. Geological Survey water-tracking programs through 2028 and updates rules for federal stream gauges.
summary.what_it_does: This law renews three U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) programs through fiscal year 2028: the Federal Priority Streamgage program, which measures water flow in major rivers and streams; a groundwater monitoring program, including the National Groundwater Monitoring Network; and grants for new ways to estimate, measure, and monitor water. It renames the National Streamflow Information Program as the Federal Priority Streamgage program. It requires that the water-quality sensors on stream gauges be precipitation water-quality sensors. It also requires each gauge site to match federal needs identified through regular outreach and feedback, such as a 2022 USGS report on program priorities.

who_it_affects.how: The agency is authorized to keep running these water monitoring and grant programs through 2028 and must follow new rules for gauge sensors and site selection.

who_it_affects.group: Groups that apply for water technology grants
who_it_affects.how: Grants for developing water estimation, measurement, and monitoring tools remain authorized through 2028.

who_it_affects.group: People and agencies that rely on flood and drought data
who_it_affects.how: Stream and groundwater monitoring that tracks water levels and conditions like floods and droughts continues under the renewed programs.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; programs are reauthorized through fiscal year 2028.
